subject: Operational commitments rider / order form language — clarity and next steps
messages:
From: Ethan Rivers <ethan.r@medisolve.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@medisolve.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: operational commitments rider + order form language

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Procurement has been asked to lock down explicit operational commitments (uptime and P95 latency) in the order form and in an attached rider to the MSA. Their asks are:

- A 99.95% monthly availability target for the dedicated model endpoint (region us-east-1).
- P95 latency at or below 220ms for single-token generation on the dedicated tier (50-token primes).
- Credit schedule for breach (tiered credit, not a full termination right).
- A short list of acceptable audit evidence (calendarized uptime report + access to historical latency histograms for the last 90 days).

Can you confirm Redwood can bind to these numbers in an order form exhibit or if we need an availability rider with carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and force majeure? Procurement prefers explicit language rather than vague SLA references. I attached a template of what their legal team circulated (see attached).

Thanks — need to move quick for the internal steering committee on Friday.

Best,
Ethan
Procurement Lead, Medisolve
attachments: template_procurement_sla_ask.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Rivers <ethan.r@medisolve.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: operational commitments rider + order form language

Ethan — thanks. Quick read-through: nothing impossible here but a couple of asks to align on before we draft language.

- 99.95% monthly availability on Dedicated is aggressive but feasible with reserved capacity + regional fallback; we need to call out maintenance windows (we typically carve out scheduled maintenance and emergency maintenance with notice windows).
- P95 220ms depends on model, request distribution, and size of the pool — can we confirm target model family and expected qps?
- Evidence: we can provide uptime reports and aggregated latency histograms; access to raw telemetry would need an NDA addendum (we can provide aggregated CSVs or stored artifacts).

I’m looping Olga (AM) to coordinate the order form wording and proposed rider. Olga — can you take the lead on a short exhibit + an orderform redline? I’ll flag this with Solutions so we have accurate perf profiles.

- Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Rivers <ethan.r@medisolve.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:23:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: operational commitments rider + order form language

Ethan — thanks for the clarity and the template. I reviewed with Product Ops and Legal and propose the following path so we can close before your steering committee: 

Plan:
1) Redwood to provide an "Operational Commitments Rider" as an MSA exhibit that enumerates: availability definition, measurement windows, latency measurement methodology (P95 over 5-minute sampling windows), exceptions (scheduled maintenance, customer-caused incidents, force majeure), and a limited credit schedule.
2) Include a short Order Form Exhibit (one page) that lists the endpoint SKU(s), region, capacity reservation (pool size), and the effective SLA numbers (99.95 / P95 220ms). Order Form will reference the Rider by exhibit id.
3) Evidence package: monthly uptime report (PDF), and a monthly latency histogram snapshot (CSV). For telemetry deeper than that we can agree to provide aggregated exports under a data-access addendum; no direct raw telemetry access.

Open questions for you:
- Confirm which model(s) will be in scope (family and tokenizer length assumptions).
- Expected steady-state QPS and burst characteristics (helps validate P95).
- Any mandatory notice period for scheduled maintenance you need us to avoid?

I attached two drafts: a short rider (proposed_operational_rider_v1.pdf) and a redline order form (orderform_redlines_medisolve.docx). Please review and we'll iterate quickly.

Next steps: If these drafts look acceptable, we’ll route to Legal for a quick MSA exhibit sign-off and then generate a DocuSign packet with the Order Form and Rider.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_operational_rider_v1.pdf; orderform_redlines_medisolve.docx

From: Ethan Rivers <ethan.r@medisolve.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@medisolve.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2028 15:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: operational commitments rider + order form language

Olga / Ben — thank you, that plan is exactly what the steering committee was asking for. A few clarifications and acceptance notes from Procurement: 

- In scope model: "rdw-dedicated-pro-13b" (single-token measurements, 50-token prompt context).
- Expected steady-state: 12 QPS with occasional bursts to 50 QPS for short windows (under 10 minutes).
- Maintenance: Procurement asks for at least 72 hours' advance notice for scheduled maintenance that would impact availability; emergency maintenance carve-outs are acceptable with post-facto reporting.
- Evidence: aggregated CSV latency snapshots + monthly PDF uptime report are acceptable.

Please proceed to route the rider to Legal. Once Redwood confirms language for the emergency maintenance carve-out and the 72-hour notice clause, Procurement will approve the DocuSign packet and we can sign the Order Form.

Thanks again — can you put target sign-off date as Feb 25?

Best,
Ethan
Procurement Lead, Medisolve
attachment: none
